content.content:
# Product page: Trail Runner 2

A product page for our new trail running shoe, Trail Runner 2, on the Stride online store. The store is already a React app with a homepage that links to `/products/trail-runner-2`; build the product page at that address, using mock data, and don't add any packages to the app beyond React and its build tool. For the look, you can take inspiration from this design:

![Trail Runner 2 product page](design.jpg)

- **Store:** the shopper sees the store name and how many items are in their cart.
- **Path:** the shopper sees where the shoe sits in the store, such as Shop, Trail, Trail Runner 2, and can go back to any earlier step.
- **Photos:** the shopper sees one photo of the shoe at a time and can move to the next or previous one, going back to the first after the last.
- **Price:** the shopper sees the price and can point at a small "i" next to it to learn that it includes taxes.
- **Color:** the shopper can choose blue, black or grey; only the chosen color shows until they change it, each with a round swatch.
- **Size:** the shopper picks one size from a list that only opens when they want to change it; only the chosen size shows, and sold-out sizes can't be picked.
- **Size guide:** the shopper can open a size chart over the page from next to the size, enter their foot length and choose US or EU to get their size, and must close it to continue.
- **Quantity:** the shopper can choose how many pairs to buy, typing the number or changing it by one.
- **Add to cart:** the shopper adds the shoe to the cart and sees a confirmation; without a size they are asked to pick one.
- **Wishlist:** the shopper can save or unsave the shoe with a heart.
- **More information:** details, reviews and shipping sit side by side below everything, with one section shown at a time.
- **Questions:** a few common questions about the shoe, each with its answer hidden until the shopper opens it.
- **Bottom of the page:** the shopper finds customer help, company and social media links.
----

Most checks pass. Four fail:

1. **Escape doesn't dismiss the price tooltip when it's opened by hover.** The keydown listener sits on the wrapper, so it only fires when focus is inside it. Escape needs a document-level listener while the tooltip is visible.

4. **axe flags the cart link** because its `aria-label` doesn't contain the visible count text. I'll put the count in the visible text and the link name.

I'll investigate 2 and 3 before changing anything.

content.text:
The product page is at `/products/trail-runner-2`. It installs, builds and starts without errors, and I checked it in Chromium: all 60 scripted checks pass, the axe-core scan finds no WCAG 2.2 AA violations (page and open size guide), and there are no console errors.

**What's there**
- **Store header:** the store name and a cart link showing the item count, which goes up when you add to cart.
- **Breadcrumb:** Shop / Trail / Trail Runner 2. The last item is the current page; the earlier steps are links.
- **Photos:** one at a time, with previous and next buttons that wrap around.
- **Price:** the price with an "i" that shows "Price includes taxes." on hover or focus, and closes on Escape.
- **Color:** only the chosen color shows. "Change color" opens three round swatches (blue, black, grey). The photos change with the color.
- **Size:** only the chosen size shows. "Change size" opens the list; sold-out sizes are disabled and labelled. Escape or choosing a size closes it.
- **Size guide:** a modal dialog with a size chart. Enter a foot length, pick US or EU, and it shows the size. "Select US 9" sets the size and closes the dialog. Closing it returns focus to the size guide button.
- **Quantity:** typed or changed with − and +, limited to 1–10.
- **Add to cart:** without a size, it asks you to pick one, opens the size list and moves focus there. Otherwise it adds to the cart and shows a confirmation.
- **Wishlist:** a toggle button (`aria-pressed`) to save or unsave.
- **Questions:** four FAQ items, each collapsed until opened.
- **More information:** Details, Reviews and Shipping & returns as tabs (arrow keys, Home and End), one panel shown at a time.
- **Footer:** customer help, company links and social links.

**Accessibility**
- Skip link, landmarks, one `h1`, and an explicit document title.
- Visible focus rings, targets at least 24px (most are 44px), and no sticky header that could hide focused elements.
- Error messages are tied to their fields. Status messages are announced politely.
- The layout works at 320px with no horizontal scrolling.

**Things to know**
- **Photos are generated placeholders.** The repo has no product photos, so I made simple SVG shoe illustrations in `public/images/`, one set per color. Swap in real photos by changing `src/data/product.js`.
- **Mock links lead nowhere yet.** The breadcrumb "Trail" link (`/shop/trail`), the footer links and the cart link (`/cart`) point to pages that don't exist; they show the app's "Page not found" text.
- **No packages were added.** The browser test tools live in `/tmp/e2e`, outside the repo.
- **Nothing is committed.** The new files are untracked; `git status` shows them alongside the change to `src/main.jsx`.
- **Preview server left running.** `npm start` (Vite preview on port 4173) is still up; stop it when you're done.
